issues.description: Method simulate(self, qc) for Exercise 1 (GroverTwoQubitWithoutAuxiliaryQubit) has inconsistent return-type contract across artifacts: the Problem Statement (Exercise 1.6) explicitly instructs students to "Simulate the circuit and return the statevector"; the template implementation's method signature is annotated as returning dict[str, int] (measurement counts) and its stub docstring likewise mismatches the statement; the reference solution's simulate() returns a statevector (signature -> list[complex] and implementation calls statevector simulator and returns result.get_statevector). This difference (problem statement expects a statevector, template hints counts, solution returns statevector) will confuse students about what to implement and what the autograded tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the simulate() contract consistent. Preferred fix: update the template to match the problem statement and reference solution by changing the simulate() return annotation and docstring to indicate it returns the statevector (e.g. -> list[complex] or -> qiskit.quantum_info.Statevector) and include a short hint/example showing how to obtain it (use Aer.get_backend('statevector_simulator') and result.get_statevector(qc)). If autograding expects measurement counts instead, then update the problem statement and the reference solution to require/return counts and change the template accordingly. Ensure tests and documentation are updated to the chosen consistent contract.
